Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph 07 CILG OPINION NO. 03 ATTY. MICHAEL T. UMALI Corporate Counsel Citinickel Mines and Development Corporation 1916 Taft Avenue, Pasay City Dear Atty. Umali: This has reference to your letter dated 23 September 2019 requesting for this Department's legal opinion relative to the imposition of business tax on a mining company by a municipality where said mining company has no branch or sales outlet in. You mentioned in your letter that the company you represent, Citinickel Mines and Development Corporation (CMDC), entered into a Mineral Sharing Agreement with the Government of the Republic of the Philippines. The said agreement permits CMDC to undertake sustainable mining operations for and on behalf of the Government subject to division of total sale. It is also stated that CMDC's principal office is in Pasay City, where the sales of the minerals extracted are all being done. The question submitted therein is, in verbatim, whether or not CMDC may be required to pay business taxes in municipalities where it deploys employees and where it does not maintain a branch or sales outlet. It is posited that the principal office is in Pasay City and it does not maintain a branch or sales outlet in Narra, Palawan, thus, the business tax of CMDC should be paid in Pasay City only. Referred in the said letter is this Department's legal opinion No. 69, series of 2018 dated 26 September 2018, wherein we opined that for the municipality/city to collect business taxes, the same should be a branch or sales office where actual sales/transactions were conducted and not merely an administrative office. This is based in the Court of Tax Appeals case i.e. City of Makati vs. The Municipality of Bakun and Luzon Hydro Corporation,l which is referred thereto. Our view is that CMDC is still liable to pay business taxes in Narra, Palawan based on the allocations set forth in Republic Act No. 7160 (RA 7160), otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991. We find Section 150(b) and (e) of RA 7160 applicable. They respectively state: Section 150. Situs of the Tax. - CTA EB case No. 1179

(a) For purposes of collection of the taxes under Section 143 of this Code, manufacturers, assemblers, repackers, brewers, distillers, rectifiers and compounders of liquor, distilled spirits and wines, millers, producers, exporters, wholesalers, distributors, dealers, contractors, banks and other financial institutions, and other businesses, maintaining or operating branch or sales outlet elsewhere shall record the sale in the branch or sales outlet making the sale or transaction, and the tax thereon shall accrue and shall be paid to the municipality where such branch or sales outlet is located. In cases where there is no such branch or sales outlet in the city or municipality where the sale or transaction is made, the sale shall be duly recorded in the principal office and the taxes due shall accrue and shall be paid to such city or municipality. (b) The following sales allocation shall apply to manufacturers, assemblers, contractors, producers, and exporters with factories, project offices, plants, and plantations in the pursuit of their business: (I) Thirty percent (30%) of all sales recorded in the principal office shall be taxable by the city or municipality where the principal office is located; and (2) Seventy percent (700/0) of all sales recorded in the principal office shall be taxable by the city or municipality where the factory, project office, plant, or plantation is located. (c) In case ofa plantation located at a place other than the place where the factory is located, said seventy percent (70%) mentioned in subparagraph (b) of subsection (2) above shall be divided as follows: (I) Sixty percent (60%) to the city or municipality where the factory is located; and (2) Forty percent (40%) to the city or municipality where the plantation is located. (d) In cases where a manufacturer, assembler, producer, exporter or contractor has two (2) or more factories, project offices, plants, or plantations located in different localities, the seventy percent (70%) sales allocation mentioned in subparagraph (b) of subsection (2) above shall be prorated among the localities where the factories, project offices, plants, and plantations are located in proportion to their respective volumes of production during the period for which the tax is due.

(e) The foregoing sales allocation shall be applied irrespective of whether or not sales are made in the locality where the factory, project office, plant, or plantation is located. Since CMDC can be classified as a contractor with a project office with factories, project offices, plants, and plantations in the pursuit of their business, then such allocation as aforementioned is applicable. Thus, 30% of the sales recorded in the principal office shall be taxable by Pasay City and that 70% of the sales recorded in the principal office shall be taxable by Municipality of Narra, Palawan. This is strengthened by the Section 150(e) as aforecited when it provides that this shall be applied whether or not sales are made in the locality where the factory, project office, plant, or plantation is located. Therefore, regardless if there are or are not sales made in the Municipality of Narra, then such allocation shall still be made applicable. It is herein emphasized that DILG Legal Opinion No. 69, series of 2018 involves an administrative office, whereas it is not in this case. What is involved herein is a contractor with a project office, factories, plants, and plantations in the pursuit of their business. Thus, we are of the opinion that said DILG opinion is not applicable to this case. Notwithstanding, let it be stressed that this legal opinion is without prejudice to a more authoritative view from the Bureau of Local Government Finance — Department of Finance which has a mandate and technical expertise over local taxation matters. Thank you. Very truly yours, By the authority of the Secretary MARIVEL C. SACENDONCILLO Undersecret ry for Local Government LLLS/42
